integrity: `sha256sum -c holdout/HASHES.sha256` gives OK for all 12 files (ANSWER_KEY, PREREGISTRATION, WORLD, CONCEPTS, K_calibration, P1–P7). Caveat: HASHES.sha256 has mtime 13:09:43, the same 70 ms window in which all seven agents/*.json were written. The only hash file therefore proves 'unchanged since the outputs were saved'. It cannot show that the answer key was 'hashed before persona runs', as log.jsonl claims at 11:10. File mtimes put prereg/key at 13:03, which is before the agent files, so the order is consistent but not proven. The log.jsonl timestamps (11:00–11:15 for FRAME to CONSTRUCT) do not match the file mtimes (13:03–13:04) and look written after the fact.

per_R.R1: PARTIAL (0.5). Pred 2: 'I answer both the same day from memory in one 2-minute reply'. Pred 1: framing 'within a few hours'. It gets the kind of answer right (quick, from memory) but predicts hours or same day, not the observed 10–15 minutes.
per_R.R2: PREDICTED (1). Pred 4: 'Nobody knows the opted-in or reachable count… Those stay blank or end up as a guess.' Mismatch: it predicts first-reply time WOULD be answered ('replies within an hour in shop hours'), but in reality it could not be. Proxy use by the consultant was not predicted.
per_R.R3: PREDICTED (1). Pred 5: Odoo export is 'most likely to be delayed or come back wrong… takes 2–3 days'. Pred 6: Google Ads 'stalls for a week'. The Meta next-day arrival was not mentioned.
per_R.R4: NOT PREDICTED (0). Pred 8 predicts the CONSULTANT widening the scope and the client resisting or accepting it ('this is getting bigger than I asked'). In reality the CLIENT reframed the goal (to reducing ride-on dependence). Different direction and different actor.
per_R.R5: PREDICTED (1). Pred 5: 'can't you just connect to Odoo / Shopify yourself?'. Pred 6: 'give me a Connect Google button'. This is circular: WORLD.md already says P1 'can connect Google accounts but hates manual exports'.
per_R.R6: NOT PREDICTED (0). Pred 6: 'I won't run a script.' It predicts refusal. In reality the client ran the script, it failed, and fixing it took back-and-forth.

decision.winner: B (wins on the primary criterion outright, so no tie-break is needed. B also has the fewest stuck points and the lowest P7 minutes. The lead's tally in log.jsonl matches.)
decision.veto: No inherent veto on B. P6 lists B blockers as 'No inherent blockers in the concept', plus 6 fixable items. One is marked 'Fixable, critical': heading hierarchy and landmarks. The others: announce dynamic questions and errors in a persistent way, not a toast; unique accessible names for Edit/Upload; tracker icons need text and aria-current; example files as text; charts need data tables. P3's B walkthrough has no Arabic blocker inherent to the concept. Its stuck points are a missing security/hosting statement for IT, no 'awaiting IT approval' state, and uncertain Arabic Word formal quality. All are fixable. Under rule 4, B cannot ship as-is until P6's fixable-critical items are fixed. That is a 'fix', not a rank-out. Note that A and C have conditional 'BLOCKER if…' items from P6.

validity: The design ranking (B > A ≈ C) can claim at most Level B (internal realism). T1 passed, so the ranking is not downgraded to anecdotal. T2 failed (3.5/6), so P1's design opinions are discounted (B still wins without P1, 3 to 0 to 0). C-partial cannot be claimed for the ranking. At most it applies to the individual P1 behaviours that matched real replay (R2, R3, R5, with R1 partial), and R3/R5 are partly circular because WORLD.md encodes them. Level C is not claimed and would need a real usability test (5 real users per client type). Persona explanations are hypotheses only.
leakage_or_violations: No answer-key leakage found. A grep of all agents/*.json for ride-on, answer key, holdout, K1–K8/R1–R6 labels, proxy, Meta export, GMC/GSC found nothing. No persona uses the key's wording for R4 or R6. In fact P1 got both wrong, which argues against leakage.

P1.note says 'Task 1 was written after reading only WORLD.md', but its replay predictions cite C1–C7, 'PORTAL' and '4 parked items'. These come from the real 002 evidence request and 003 message, not WORLD.md. That access is allowed by prereg T2, but the note is inaccurate. log.jsonl round-1 inputs list only world/WORLD.md and designs/, so P1's real input allowlist is undocumented.
P7 refers to P1/P5/P6 by ID and to other personas' constraints. This is allowed because WORLD.md is shared and P7 'sees all engagements'. It does mean P7 is not blind to the other personas' profiles.

Personas add invented specifics that are not in their files (P1: Abu Dhabi cut-off, stock-counter app, 2 WhatsApp phones). These are plausible persona confabulation, not leakage, and should be treated as hypotheses.
Process: the claim that the answer key was 'hashed before persona runs' cannot be verified (see integrity). Log timestamps do not match file mtimes.
notes: T1 shows a ceiling effect, so it is a weak validity test. K_calibration.md describes its defects almost literally ('There is no button', 'can't be saved part-way', 'red dot', 'Nothing else'), so 7/7 personas found K3–K8 and even non-accessibility personas found K5/K8. Detection at 100% pooled and 7.29/8 average does little to tell sensitive raters from insensitive ones. K2 (no reason per file) was the only discriminating defect, found only by P1 and P7. K8 scoring was lenient: P1, P2, P4 and P5 named 'drag-and-drop only, no button' through phone or trackpad reasons, not keyboard. Under a strict keyboard-only reading only P3, P6 and P7 hit K8, which would drop those four personas to 6 or 7 hits. That does not change the pass. Extras: about 20 distinct valid issues beyond the key. Examples: no how-to-get-it steps, no connect-account option, no delegate / don't-have / pending-approval route, no visible human or approval gate, no Arabic/RTL, no data-security statement, a dataset list that doesn't fit the domain, trade licence not applicable to government or pre-revenue, 3-second transient toast, asterisk-only required markers, no headings/landmarks/error summary, no data as-of date or provenance capture, no upload receipt, no price shown, no second user for an analyst, no number sourcing, and fixed KPI/constraint counts that force filler. Six of the six client personas say 'with_help' or 'yes' on B only through fixable gaps. P2 and P3 are 'with_help' on all concepts because of entity approval rules, so that is a world constraint, not a design flaw. Recommend red-teaming the possibility of designer bias: CONCEPTS.md describes B with noticeably more fixes for the known pain points (why/how-to/invite/autosave/next-step) than A or C.
